item.title: Florida execution warrant signed for 1998 child murder case
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Gov. Ron DeSantis has signed an execution warrant for a man convicted in a 1998 child killing, marking what would be the 22nd execution carried out in Florida this year, according to reporting from North Escambia. The development comes as a group of death row exonerees has appealed to Florida's next governor to reconsider the state's accelerated…
item.content:encoded:
Gov. Ron DeSantis has signed an execution warrant for a man convicted in a 1998 child killing, marking what would be the 22nd execution carried out in Florida this year, according to reporting from North Escambia.

The development comes as a group of death row exonerees has appealed to Florida's next governor to reconsider the state's accelerated pace of executions. The exonerated individuals, who spent years on death row before being released, have raised concerns about the speed at which capital sentences are being carried out.

Florida has become one of the nation's most active states in executing death row inmates, with the pace raising questions among criminal justice advocates about due process and the reliability of convictions in older cases.

item.title: Cold Front Brings Frost Risk, Sunny Skies to North Escambia This Weekend
item.dc:creator: newsroom

After Thursday reaches a pleasant high near 74 degrees, temperatures will plummet for the remainder of the weekend. Friday and Saturday highs are expected to settle in the upper 50s…
item.content:encoded:
A cold front moving through North Escambia today will bring a significant shift in weather conditions, delivering dry skies and noticeably colder air by week's end.

After Thursday reaches a pleasant high near 74 degrees, temperatures will plummet for the remainder of the weekend. Friday and Saturday highs are expected to settle in the upper 50s and low 60s, with frost likely developing overnight as clear skies allow temperatures to drop further.

The dry, sunny conditions accompanying the cold front should provide ideal weather for outdoor activities during the day, though residents planning to spend time outside early mornings or evenings should prepare for much cooler conditions. Anyone with sensitive plants or outdoor preparations should take precautions against frost damage Friday and Saturday nights.

item.content:encoded: Matt Dannheisser, who has served as Century's town attorney for more than three decades, has stepped down effective immediately, citing difficulties with the municipality's senior leadership. According to reporting from North Escambia, Dannheisser's departure marks the end of a lengthy tenure representing the small North Escambia community. The town has already begun the process of bringing in interim legal counsel to fill the gap left by his resignation. Mayor Ben Boutwell and the five-member town council received Dannheisser's resignation letter via email. The specific nature of the workplace conflicts that prompted his exit was not detailed in the initial announcement, but the sudden nature of the departure and the swift move to find replacement counsel suggest the situation had become untenable for both sides.

item.title: Historic SS United States Departs for Final Voyage, Scuttled at Sea
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: The SS United States, a legendary ocean liner that carried presidents and celebrities across the Atlantic, departed Thursday for what will be its final resting place at the bottom of the sea. According to WKRG-TV 5, historians and former passengers gathered to bid farewell to the vessel as it left port, marking the end of an era for one of…
item.content:encoded:
The SS United States, a legendary ocean liner that carried presidents and celebrities across the Atlantic, departed Thursday for what will be its final resting place at the bottom of the sea. According to WKRG-TV 5, historians and former passengers gathered to bid farewell to the vessel as it left port, marking the end of an era for one of America's most iconic ships.

The SS United States, which set the transatlantic speed record when it launched in 1952, has been a floating museum and tourist attraction in recent years. The decision to scuttle the ship—intentionally sinking it in a designated deepwater location—comes after efforts to preserve or repurpose the vessel proved economically unfeasible.

The ship's final voyage carries historical weight for those who sailed aboard her during her heyday and for maritime historians who viewed her as a symbol of American engineering and design. The scuttling process will turn the ship into an artificial reef, creating a new marine habitat while ending decades of uncertainty about the vessel's future.

The ship, which sat anchored about 22 miles off the coast of Destin Harbor, drew onlookers determined to witness a piece of naval history before its fate is…
item.content:encoded:
Hundreds of people lined up in Destin on Wednesday to catch a final glimpse of the SS United States, the iconic ocean liner that once represented the height of American maritime travel. The ship, which sat anchored about 22 miles off the coast of Destin Harbor, drew onlookers determined to witness a piece of naval history before its fate is decided.

The SS United States, launched in 1952, was a symbol of American engineering and luxury travel during the golden age of ocean liners. The vessel held the transatlantic speed record for decades and carried presidents, celebrities, and thousands of everyday passengers across the Atlantic.

According to WKRG News 5, the gathering reflected the emotional connection many people have to the historic ship. Despite the distance from shore and the wait involved in viewing the vessel, attendees showed up to say goodbye to a maritime landmark that represented an era of American innovation and elegance.

item.title: SS United States sunk off Florida panhandle to become world's largest artificial reef
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: The SS United States, an iconic ocean liner, has been intentionally sunk off Florida's Gulf Coast to create the world's largest artificial reef, according to reports from CBS News and the Pensacola News Journal. The vessel, which was being scuttled off the coast of Florida's panhandle, completed its final journey Thursday as crews executed the…
item.content:encoded:
The SS United States, an iconic ocean liner, has been intentionally sunk off Florida's Gulf Coast to create the world's largest artificial reef, according to reports from CBS News and the Pensacola News Journal.

The vessel, which was being scuttled off the coast of Florida's panhandle, completed its final journey Thursday as crews executed the controlled sinking. Officials confirmed the ship was fully submerged as part of the planned operation.

The project transforms the historic liner—once a symbol of American maritime travel—into a marine habitat that will support fish populations and diving tourism in the region. The artificial reef is expected to attract divers and support local marine ecosystems in the waters off Northwest Florida.

item.content:encoded:
The SS United States, a legendary ocean liner that spent decades moored in Philadelphia, is being deliberately sunk off the coast of Pensacola today to create an artificial reef, according to posts circulating on social media.

The vessel, which once served as a flagship of American maritime travel, will become one of the largest artificial reefs in the world upon completion of the scuttling operation. The ship had been docked at a Philadelphia port for many years before the decision was made to sink it in local waters.

The sinking is being documented and livestreamed, offering Pensacola residents and maritime enthusiasts a chance to witness the historic moment. The transformation of the ship into an underwater reef is expected to provide habitat for marine life and potentially become a destination for divers in the future.

item.content:encoded:
Santa Rosa County motorists should expect intermittent lane closures on Nichols Lake Road beginning tomorrow, starting Thursday, November 12. The work zone will be located between Sawyer Road and Dawn Drive, just east of Highway 87, as contractor C.W. Roberts Contracting installs a new turn lane for a subdivision development project.

County officials say flaggers will be positioned at each end of the work area to direct traffic and improve safety. Drivers passing through should exercise caution and be prepared for possible delays during construction hours.

According to Santa Rosa County, the project is slated to wrap up by December 18, weather permitting. For a detailed map of the affected area, Santa Rosa County has posted resources on its website.

item.content:encoded:
Two local artists are launching Recreation Art Supply, a pop-up shop designed to make creative materials more accessible and affordable for Pensacola's art community. Reema Eqab and Raylene Solis are centralizing used art supplies to lower the cost barrier for aspiring and established creatives who might otherwise struggle to afford traditional retail prices.

The concept addresses a real gap in the local market — quality art materials can be expensive, and the pop-up model allows the pair to test the idea while building community support. By focusing on used and repurposed supplies, Recreation Art Supply also promotes sustainability while serving artists across skill levels.

The shop reflects growing interest in Pensacola's creative economy and grassroots entrepreneurship. For anyone in the area looking for affordable art supplies or wanting to support local artists, the pop-up offers both practical access and a chance to connect with the creative community.

item.content:encoded:
The Pensacola Opera is reviving its Brown Bag Opera program, offering locals a chance to enjoy arias and theater selections during their lunch break, according to a news release reported by WKRG News 5.

The series brings live opera performance to a casual, accessible format — attendees can bring their own lunch and enjoy professional opera in an informal setting. The next Brown Bag Opera performance is scheduled for Tuesday, November 18.

The return of the program marks another offering from the Pensacola Opera's community engagement lineup, giving music and theater enthusiasts an opportunity to experience live performance without the formality of a full evening at the opera house.
